In the triangle above, what is the length of $\overset{―}{AC}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165760/assets/277e019b26f72cffd7647abe694338acd099e4d48fc532a7e9d6ad362a49dcc9.png)

Since this is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the shorter leg has length $x=6$ and the longer leg has length $\sqrt{3}x,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{AC}=\sqrt{3}x=\sqrt{3}\cdot 6=6\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the longer leg is $6\sqrt{3}.$
